title:
Someone is now hiring
for the role the
*AI era* created.
sub: A recruiter sent me the job description this week. No names — just the signal.

title: What the role actually is:
text:
An embedded quality authority who sits *inside* the AI and data-science teams, not outside them.

In sprint reviews, architecture discussions and stage-gate decisions — not only at the formal quality checkpoint at the end.

title:
From reviewer
to participant.
text: Validation used to arrive after the build. This role arrives at inception — naming the controls, the risks and the mitigations while the model is still being shaped.

title:
What they expect
you to know:
items: *Model types* — classical ML, deep learning, LLMs, vision, NLP
*The stack* — training, fine-tuning, RAG, prompting, evaluation
*AI failure modes* — bias, drift, hallucination, explainability, lineage
*The regulations* — Part 11, GAMP 5 2nd ed, Annex 11, ICH Q9(R1), CSA, EU AI Act
*The judgment* — right-sized control for each use case

title: Read that list again.
text:
Half of it isn't CSV. It's data science.

The ask is for validation people who can hold a real conversation with engineers — and be credible while doing it.

title:
They want someone
comfortable slowing
things down.
text:
It is written into the qualifications — the person in the room whose job is occasionally to say not yet.

That isn't a documentation skill. That's standing.
tag: Hard to hire. Harder to fake.

title:
A live inventory of
AI use cases.
text:
Every AI initiative, its current validation and control status, visible to leadership.

Not an annual system list. A standing view of where AI is influencing GxP decisions right now.
tag: Most orgs cannot produce this today

title: What this tells us:
text:
The market has stopped debating whether AI belongs in GxP.

It is now hiring on the assumption that AI is already in the building — and that somebody has to be accountable for how it gets used.

title:
If you work in CSV,
this is your window:
items: *Learn the vocabulary* — enough to ask a data scientist a real question
*Practise proportionality* — not every use case earns the full package
*Produce decisions, not documents* — proceed, control, validate, refuse
*Get in the room early* — a review at the end is a review too late

title:
If you lead QA or IT,
three questions:
items: How many AI use cases touch a GxP decision today?
For each one, who decided the level of control was proportionate?
Could we show an inspector that reasoning — this week?

title:
Has your org started the
AI-in-GxP journey?
text:
Forward this to your QA, CSV or IT lead — this is the role they're about to be asked to fill, or to become.

Questions welcome in the comments.
